name: Natural Images Classification
tagline: Comparing CNN and transfer learning on eight image classes
meta: University of East London · Artificial Intelligence & Machine Vision · CN7023
lede: I compared a custom convolutional neural network with ResNet50 and DenseNet121 on the Natural Images dataset, using TensorFlow to prepare, augment and evaluate the image data.
highlights: Worked with eight classes: airplane, car, cat, dog, flower, fruit, motorbike and person; split the data into 70% training, 15% validation and 15% test sets.
Resized images to 128 × 128 pixels, rescaled pixel values and used flips, rotation, zoom and contrast adjustments for augmentation.
Compared a custom CNN with transfer-learning models ResNet50 and DenseNet121.
Reported test-set accuracy: custom CNN 83.80%, DenseNet121 99.14% and ResNet50 99.81%; the report gives ResNet50 a loss of 0.0089.
The coursework report found the custom CNN confused visually similar cat and dog images; the transfer-learning models performed better on the reported test set.

name: AWS Warehouse Architecture
tagline: A layered AWS design for warehouse inventory workflows
meta: University of East London · Cloud Computing · CN7026 · 2026/27
lede: I designed a cloud architecture for warehouse automation and inventory management, separating user traffic, application processing and data storage across AWS services.
highlights: Mapped requirements for inventory updates, data storage, access control, alerts, scalability, security and availability.
Designed a VPC with public and private subnets, EC2, Lambda, RDS for PostgreSQL, S3, DynamoDB, SQS, CloudWatch and IAM; the project plan also covered SNS, load balancing and Auto Scaling.
Proposed a multi-Availability-Zone design in the us-east-1 region, with warehouse scanners, sensors and applications feeding the cloud workflow.

Early AWS setup encountered IAM permission errors when configuring services. The report identifies access-policy configuration as an implementation challenge; this was an academic architecture project, not a production deployment.
